fixes.explanation: Jerusalem is right, friend. Verse 13 says John left them at Perga to return there. The text doesn't tell us why he went, so I'm not guessing out loud. I'll just say that when a teammate heads back mid-journey, the rest of the crew still has dough to roll.

False is right. The leaders don't say a word about staying quiet. They send word in verse 15: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.” Two visitors just sat down, and they got handed the floor.

That's a sensible guess, because Jerusalem was just mentioned in verse 13. But the leaders never ask for a report. Verse 15 says they ask for “…a word of encouragement for the people…” No status update in this verse, friend, just encouragement.

The reading already happened, though. Verse 15 says this invitation comes after the reading from the Law and the Prophets. What the leaders ask for next is “…a word of encouragement for the people…” So the request is for words of encouragement, not another reading.
That's it. Paul says, “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!” (Acts 13:16). So he addresses two groups in one room, and he speaks to both at once.
True. Paul says in verse 18, “He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.” Forty years, friend. Say it out loud and it sounds even longer.

Samuel is in this passage, but as a prophet, not the king. Verse 20 names him as the prophet whose time the judges lasted until. The king in verse 22 is “…David son of Jesse…” Samuel's father was Elkanah (1 Samuel 1:19, 20), so you've got your sons and fathers all lined up, friend, just not the king in this verse.

That's not how Paul tells it. Acts 13:31 says that for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Then Paul says, “They are now His witnesses to our people.” So Paul points to the people who traveled with Him as the ones who saw Him.

Jerusalem came up earlier in the passage, but not here. Verse 42 says the people urged Paul and Barnabas to continue this message on the next Sabbath. The request is about when, the next Sabbath, and the verse doesn't mention Jerusalem.

Grace is right, friend. Verse 43 says Paul and Barnabas spoke to the many Jews and devout converts who followed them, and urged them to continue in the grace of God. Just before that, in verse 39, Paul said that through Jesus everyone who believes is justified. Grace is a good word to carry out of a synagogue, and I'd stitch it on my apron if I had the room.
The temple is a natural guess, since this crowd knows its worship places. But Acts 13:43 says Paul and Barnabas urged them to continue in the grace of God. So the blank holds grace, not a building.

Jealousy is right. Verse 44 says nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord. Then verse 45 says when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy. I think that's a hard moment to read.

Sorrow would make the story softer, but it isn't the word. Verse 45 says when the Jews saw the crowds, “…they were filled with jealousy…” The same verse goes on to say they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying. The text gives us jealousy.
That's not how it goes. Verse 46 says Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly. The text doesn't say they backed down. They go on to say, “…we now turn to the Gentiles.”
False is right. Acts 13:46 says Paul and Barnabas “…answered them boldly…” They don't back down. They go on to say, “…we now turn to the Gentiles.”

That phrase shows up in Isaiah 40:3, so I see where it came from. But in Acts 13:47 the Lord says, “I have made you a light for the Gentiles…” That's the line Paul and Barnabas quote. The light is the answer.

A shield is a strong picture, but it isn't the one in this verse. Acts 13:47 says, “I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.” So the answer is a light for the Gentiles. The same verse says the salvation reaches to the ends of the earth.

Right. Verse 49 says, “And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.” Verse 44 already says nearly the whole city gathered to hear it. The word covers a whole region, and it didn't need a group chat to do it.
Paul spoke in the synagogue, but verse 49 says the word of the Lord spread “…throughout that region.” It didn't stay put. So the answer is the region, not the synagogue.
That would be a short trip for news. But Acts 13:49 says the word of the Lord spread throughout that region. A whole region is a lot bigger than a gate, friend.

Right. Verse 50 says the Jews incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district. It's a heavy moment, and I think it stings a little.

The proconsul does come up earlier in Paul's journey (Acts 13:7), but this verse doesn't use him. Acts 13:50 says the persecution drove Paul and Barnabas out of their district. Nobody's hauled in front of an official here. They just have to go.

Dust is right. Verse 51 says they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them. It's a clear move, no words needed. I spent years in a junk drawer under a pile of dust, friend, and I never made a point that good with it.

Iconium is right. Verse 51 says they shook the dust off their feet and went to Iconium. So the road keeps going, and the story goes with it. The journey doesn't stop when they're driven out of a district.

Lystra comes up later in Paul's journey (Acts 14:6), but it's not where they go in this verse. Acts 13:51 says they went to Iconium. So Lystra is a good guess for the map, and still not the answer for this blank.
